# QA Plan — SYS-01 Input & Control Mapping

**Date**: 2026-11-12
**Generated by**: `/qa-plan` (system-level acceptance plan; not a sprint plan)
**Scope**: SYS-01 Input & Control Mapping — 79 ACs / 96 clause-units
**Engine**: Godot 4.7.2 / GDScript / GUT
**Authority**: SYS-01 GDD #10 diff-scoped record (`PASS WITH RECORDED
OBLIGATIONS`; review loop closed at #10; GDD unfrozen) + ADR-0001 (Accepted
2026-11-12)
**Carries**: **O1** — AC-18's stamp-budget head ("up to 2") vs its parenthetical
("p99.9 ≤ 2 and max ≤ 3"); the ratified budget is **p99.9 ≤ 2, max ≤ 3**; the
AC-65 protocol below measures it.
**Hard gate**: the 16-item engine register (AC-74) must close before the first
implementation story. The ledger may be printed now; the smoke gate executes
after the register closes.

---

## 1 · Purpose and authority

This plan is the **operational home** of the SYS-01 acceptance criteria. The GDD
states what must be true; the ADR states how; this plan states **how it is
measured**, who signs, and where the evidence lives. It is written at the
altitude the GDD's review #5 established: the GDD keeps requirement bars and
pointers; the methodology (perf workloads, estimators, sample counts, thermal
protocol, layout arithmetic, AC-64/AC-63 protocols) lives here.

**Authority chain.**

1. `design/gdd/input-control-mapping.md` — the design laws and AC text.
2. `docs/architecture/adr-0001-input-architecture.md` — the architecture and the
   five ratified laws.
3. This plan — the 96-unit AC→gate ledger and the measurement protocols.
4. `design/gdd/reviews/input-control-mapping-review-log.md` — the #10 record
   (O1) and the #8/#9 records (NB-I, NB-J, the 96-unit ledger).

**What this plan is not.** It is not a sprint plan, not a story breakdown, and
not a substitute for the GDD. It does not invent acceptance criteria; every unit
below is an AC or a clause of an AC from the GDD. It does not re-open the
review loop; the loop is closed at #10.

**Non-negotiable conventions.**

- **One gate per clause-unit.** Every AC — and every clause of a split AC —
  belongs to exactly one gate. The `[GUT]`/`[DEVICE]` tags describe where a
  clause **runs**, not which gate owns it.
- **The four gates**: MVP smoke (67), MVP device (19), MVP-lock (3), VS (7).
  Total **96**.
- **A `[DEVICE]`-tagged clause never defaults home to smoke.** The smoke gate's
  "one device pass" is a runtime sanity check on the same build, not a
  gate-membership claim.
- **No unit is counted twice.** The exactly-one proof is §2.3.
- **Evidence is a path, not a promise.** Every executed unit names a file or a
  run manifest; a unit without evidence is not done.

### 2.3 Exactly-one proof

The ledger is a partition, not a list of claims. The proof has four properties:

1. **Totality.** Every AC-01…AC-79 appears; every split clause appears. Census:
   79 ACs (no gaps, no duplicates), 65 singles + 14 splits = 31 split
   clause-units, 96 rows. Count: 67 + 19 + 3 + 7 = 96.
2. **No double-claims.** Each of the 96 rows is a distinct `(AC, clause)` pair;
   no pair appears in two gates. The gate column is a function of the pair.
3. **Manifest↔inline agreement.** Every split AC's inline `Gate split` sentence
   matches its ledger rows: AC-03 (GUT/DEVICE), AC-33 (2 smoke + 1 VS), AC-36
   (device/VS), AC-37 (device/VS), AC-47 (GUT/DEVICE), AC-48 (GUT/DEVICE),
   AC-52 (GUT/DEVICE), AC-53 (GUT/DEVICE), AC-60 (smoke/VS), AC-65 (GUT/DEVICE),
   AC-66 (GUT/DEVICE), AC-69 (VS + 3 device), AC-70 (2 device), AC-74
   (GUT/DEVICE).
4. **Discriminator.** All 17 `[DEVICE]`-tagged ACs are accounted for and none
   defaults home to smoke: AC-03, AC-12, AC-27, AC-36, AC-37, AC-45, AC-47,
   AC-48, AC-50, AC-52, AC-53, AC-64, AC-65, AC-66, AC-69, AC-70, AC-74.

**The four NB-E units** — AC-12, AC-45, AC-36's MVP clause, AC-37's MVP clause —
are **device-gated** (rows 13, 50, 39, 41). This is the explicit resolution the
#7 record required; it is not a default-home reading.

**O1 row** — AC-18 (row 19) is smoke-gated as a whole AC. The AC-18 GUT test
asserts the Early Press offer cadence (including the stamp tick); the stamp
**budget** is not measured by AC-18. The budget is measured by AC-65's device
half (row 76) when engine item 12 yields OS event time; otherwise it degrades to
the callback-arrival caveat and the budget is ADR-owned. O1's text fix is
tracked in §11.

### 2.5 What each gate means

- **MVP smoke** — "input is ready for QA hand-off." Headless GUT on the CI
  build + one device pass on the same build. Any single failure blocks hand-off.
  It is the default home for the GUT clauses and the GUT halves of the
  device-split ACs; it is not a device gate.
- **MVP device** — device-executed clauses that are not MVP-lock or VS. The
  device matrix and the per-AC protocols are §7–§9. A device failure blocks the
  MVP lock for that clause's claim.
- **MVP-lock** — the three whole-AC claims that gate the MVP lock: the
  dual-purpose-button playtest (AC-02), the coded feel rubric (AC-63), and the
  backdash producibility bars (AC-64). These run on device/playtest, not in the
  smoke gate.
- **VS** — chip and Stinger clauses. They are **not** MVP scope; the chip is a
  Reserved slot until SYS-17/SYS-24, and the Stinger recognizer is flagged out
  of MVP builds. The VS gate runs when those systems go live. Their ledger rows
  exist now so the partition is total and the future work has a home.

## 3 · Gate execution model

### 3.1 Execution order

```
0. Probe register (AC-74) — all 16 items have a verdict; zero PROBE-PENDING
1. Smoke GUT — headless, CI build; the 67 smoke units
2. Smoke device pass — one device pass on the same build (runtime sanity)
3. MVP device gate — 19 units on the device matrix
4. MVP-lock gate — AC-02, AC-63, AC-64 (device/playtest)
5. VS gate — 7 units when the chip/Stinger go live
```

The probe register is **first** because AC-74's open items block the first
implementation story. The smoke GUT runs before the device pass so a logic
failure never consumes device-lab time. The MVP-lock gate runs after the device
gate because AC-64's producibility data and AC-63's playtest cohort are the
expensive instruments; they run once the build is stable.

### 3.2 MVP smoke gate — "input is ready for QA hand-off"

**Instrument**: headless GUT on the CI build + **one device pass** on the same
build. Any single failure blocks hand-off. The GDD's 31-AC smoke list (30
bullets, AC-38/39 are two ACs):

> AC-01 · AC-07 · AC-23 · AC-17 · AC-18 · AC-19 · AC-20 · AC-21 · AC-16 ·
> AC-30 · AC-31 · AC-38/39 · AC-44 · AC-59 · AC-68 · AC-75 · AC-77 · AC-71 ·
> AC-73 · AC-72 · AC-58 · AC-25 · AC-54 · AC-53 (GUT half) · AC-10 · AC-66
> (GUT half) · AC-24 · AC-65 (GUT half) · AC-79

This list is a **subset** of the 67 smoke units: it is the critical path the GDD
names, not the whole gate. The other 36 smoke units still run in the gate; they
are not optional. The smoke list is the "must be green before hand-off" spine.

**Evidence**: a GUT XML result + console log per run; the device pass's
screenshot/video + the run manifest. Path:
`production/qa/evidence/sys01/smoke/<run-id>/`.

**Failure rule**: any single failure blocks hand-off. A flaky test is quarantined
with a recorded owner and a re-run; it does not silently pass (the
`/test-flakiness` registry).

### 3.3 MVP device gate

**Instrument**: the device matrix in §7; each clause's protocol in §8–§9. The
gate is **19 units**, not 19 ACs: AC-69 contributes three device clauses; AC-70
two; the split ACs contribute their device halves.

**Evidence**: per-AC folder with the run manifest (device SKU, OS build, density,
safe-area query, app build hash), screenshots/video, the raw trace/log. Path:
`production/qa/evidence/sys01/device/<ac>/`.

**Failure rule**: a device clause failure blocks the MVP lock for that claim. A
clause can be re-run after a fix; the re-run is a new evidence folder, not an
overwrite.

### 3.4 MVP-lock gate

| Unit | Instrument | Sign-off |
|---|---|---|
| AC-02 | Playtest cohort ≥5, ≥30 min; the dual-purpose-button question; the reproduction step | creative-director + qa-lead |
| AC-63 | Coded rubric; two facilitators; per-statement agreement ≥90%; Cohen's kappa ≥0.7 | creative-director + qa-lead |
| AC-64 | Producibility protocol; p10/false-fire/end-to-end/a11y bars; ARM fallback | creative-director + qa-lead |

**Failure rule**: any MVP-lock unit below its bar blocks MVP lock. AC-64's
fallback evaluation is for the ARM-fixable bar classes only; the timing/detector
bars are gated separately (see §7.2).

### 3.5 VS gate

The seven VS units are deferred. The chip is a Reserved slot until SYS-17/SYS-24;
the Stinger recognizer is flagged out of MVP builds (TR-INP-032). The VS gate
runs when those systems go live. The ledger rows are already assigned so the
partition stays total; the protocols are outlined in §10.

### 3.6 Evidence convention

Every executed unit names:

- **Run manifest**: build hash, engine version, device SKU/OS, density, safe
  rect, `k`, active hit-scale, mirror state, test harness version.
- **Raw evidence**: GUT XML/console, device video/screenshot, trace file, or
  playtest transcript.
- **Verdict**: PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED, with the AC row and the clause.
- **Sign-off**: qa-lead (smoke/device), creative-director + qa-lead (lock), qa-lead
  + design (VS).

A unit without a run manifest is not executed. A screenshot without the manifest
is not evidence. The run manifest is the first file in every evidence folder.

## 4 · Test architecture

### 4.1 The pure core

`InputCore` is a `RefCounted` with injected ports (ADR-0001 §15). The GUT suite
constructs it directly; no scene tree, no `Input`, no `Time`, no renderer. The
GDD's GUT testability map is the contract:

| Formula | Purity | Injected clock | Signature test |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 `ms_to_ticks` | pure fn | none | boundary table 140@60→9; exact-integer; rate matrix 30/60/120/240 |
| F-02 `stick_vector_normalization` | pure fn | none | pin-at-leash; deadzone→0; sign preservation; per-source profiles |
| F-03 `movement_band_selection` | pure reducer | none | no-chatter fuzz in both sticky zones; nesting invariant |
| F-04 `crouch_zone_test` | reducer + guard | wall-clock ms | 89 vs 90 ms; 25→45° no-pop; raw flip at the guard tick while committed |
| F-05 `intent_window_evaluation` | service | `logic_tick` | age == window honored; +1 expired; supersede restarts; freeze holds; same-tick offer |
| F-06 `hit_rect_floor` | pure fn ×2 | none | device-profile table; ceil integrality; fractional density |
| F-07 `backdash_pattern_recognition` | detector | `logic_tick` | 280 boundary; missing release; busy drop; late re-arm; entry_sign model |
| F-08 `body_busy` | pure OR | none (publishers mocked) | raise/clear mid-window; fail-open + assertion |
| F-09 `chip_commit_rule` | predicate | wall-clock ms | threshold −0.1 vs threshold; slide-off dominance |
| F-10 `interact_target_binding` | predicate | none (prompt stub) | mid-window unlight; relit ≠ stale; both-fail precedence |

### 4.2 Fakes and injection

| Port | Fake | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GameClockPort` | `FixedClock` | Set `logic_tick`/`physics_tick`; freeze/unfreeze; freeze-onset boundary |
| `StateProviderPort` | `ScriptedStateProvider` | Held keys/pad/touch; re-assertion; ownership |
| `RenderMetricsPort` | `FixedMetrics` | Safe rect, band, `k`, density; mirror; crop |
| `PromptRegistryPort` | `FakePromptRegistry` | Lit/unlit, nearest-wins, signed latch, binding |
| `BodyBusyPort` | `FakeBodyBusy` | Locks/commitments; fail-open; watchdog |
| `FacingPort` | `FakeFacing` | Value/epoch/cause; press1-induced turn; resets |
| `TuningPort` | `FakeTuning` | Knob values; V0–V21; live edits |

**Event injection.** `Input.parse_input_event(event)` for event-delivery
equivalence (key, joypad, screen touch); `Input.action_press(action, strength)`
only for state-only tests. The deadzone-0 equivalence test uses
`parse_input_event` with a real `InputEventJoypadMotion`/`InputEventScreenTouch`
and asserts the post-F-02 magnitude matches the hardware path; `action_press`
bypasses the deadzone and is not a substitute (ADR-0001 §15).

**Replay.** A `CapturedEvent` stream carries `arrival_usec`; replay through the
core with `FixedClock` and mocked pullers; compare to the human capture. The
same stream must produce the same `InputFrame`/`PulledIntent` records
(AC-07/AC-55). The replay harness is the OQ#13 "input test-harness service" —
cheap now, expensive to retrofit.

### 4.4 CI and the no-direct-Input rule

- **CI job**: headless GUT on the pinned Godot 4.7.2; the 67 smoke units; the
  GUT halves of AC-53/65/66/74. No device in CI.
- **Static audit**: a CI grep for `Input.is_action_`, `Input.get_axis`,
  `Input.get_vector`, `Input.is_action_just_pressed` outside `src/input/`.
  A hit fails the job. Consumers read `InputBus`/`InputFrame`.
- **Deadzone audit**: every SYS-01-registered action has deadzone 0 at boot
  (AC-73); the engine's `ui_*` actions are excluded.
- **Knob audit**: the Tuning Knobs table parses 55 rows / 55 distinct symbols;
  the V0–V21 fixpoint test; the live-edit re-validation test.
- **Ledger audit**: this plan's 96 rows are re-derived from the manifest; the
  exactly-one proof is a test, not a comment.

### 4.5 The smoke GUT spine

The 67 smoke units are not all in one test file; the spine the GDD names is the
critical path. The GUT runner groups them by formula/contract:

| Group | Units | Representative tests |

| Registry/verbs | AC-01, 04, 05, 06, 09, 11 | registry audit; single puller; behavior gating |
| Cross-rig | AC-07, 08, 13, 15, 29 | boot parity; replay; hot-unplug; coyote identity |
| Window/buffer | AC-14, 16…24, 30, 31, 49, 55 | F-01/F-03/F-04/F-05; OS repeat; supersede; rate matrix |
| Touch/layout | AC-25, 26, 28, 34, 47, 48, 52, 66, 76, 77 | F-06; z-order; gap/reach; bubble cascade |
| Gestures | AC-38…41, 64 | F-07; entry_sign; false-fire replay; a11y press |
| Gates | AC-43, 44, 46, 59, 62, 79 | context table; terminality; death case; first-tick delivery |
| Contracts | AC-56…58, 67, 68, 75 | derived move; body_busy; Interact; custody |
| Perf/alloc | AC-53 (GUT), 54, 65 (GUT) | pipeline structure; allocation; stamp law |
| A11y/visual | AC-51, 61, 70 (device), 71…73, 78 | no popups; haptics hooks; re-assertion; knobs; EX audit |

## 5 · Perf ledger — AC-53 / AC-54 / AC-65

The GDD keeps the requirement bars; this section is the methodology the altitude
law moved here. The bars are not restated as new requirements; they are measured
exactly as the GDD states them.

### 5.1 Reference environment and run manifest

**Reference SKU candidates** (the exact device is recorded in every run manifest;
a bar measured on an unrecorded device is not valid):

| Class | Candidate | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Android mid-range | Pixel 6a (Tensor G1, 6 GB, 60 Hz, Android 14) | The mid-range target; 60 Hz; cutout surface |
| iOS | iPhone 12 (A14, 4 GB, 60 Hz, iOS 17) | The older supported iPhone class |
| Desktop | The 4K desktop profile on integrated graphics | The 4K@2.0 windowed profile; no cutout floors |
| Low-H probe | 1440×720 px @2.75 (Android display-size scaling) | The V21 / band stress profile |

**Run manifest fields**: app build hash, Godot 4.7.2 build hash, device SKU, OS
build, display size px, density, safe rect, `k`, active hit-scale, mirror state,
battery/thermal state, probe version, workload ID, sample count.

**Release build**: the measurement runs on a release export (or a release-like
build with the probe enabled by a flag), not the editor. The probe's overhead is
measured by a null-pipeline run; if the probe's own p99.9 exceeds 0.05 ms, the
probe is optimized before the bar is trusted.

### 5.2 Workloads

| ID | Workload | Duration | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Idle (no input) | 10,000 ticks | Baseline; capture drain empty; publication only |
| W2 | Walk (stick at 0.60) | 10,000 ticks | F-02/F-03 steady state; re-assertion |
| W3 | Mash 12 t/s (Attack/Jump alternating) | 10,000 ticks | Supersede; haptic enqueue; S_base |
| W4 | Mash 4 t/s | 10,000 ticks | Pending gaps; supersede; S_base |
| W5 | Multi-touch 3 contacts (stick + Jump + Attack) | 10,000 ticks | Dispatcher; z-order; capture burst |
| W6 | Burst (5% of ticks with ≥3 concurrent arrivals) | 10,000 ticks | S_burst; non-emptiness; drain-all |
| W7 | Backdash traces (AC-64 logged traces replayed) | 10,000 ticks | F-07; entry_sign; drops |
| W8 | Gate transitions (pause/menu/resume, death) | 1,000 ticks | Gate-entry; terminality; buffers |
| W9 | Chip hold (VS) | 10,000 ticks | F-09; deferred to VS |
| W10 | Haptics-on jank (12 t/s mash + haptic stream) | 60 s | AC-70's jank clause |

The **impossible touch-3 crouch-oscillation load is deleted** (the GDD's review
#5): TR-INP-072's single-owner zone makes a third in-zone touch inert. W5 uses
three contacts in distinct regions (stick + two buttons), not three in the zone.

### 5.3 Estimators and sample counts

**Percentile convention: nearest-rank (order statistic), no interpolation.**

```
p(q) = sorted_ascending[ ceil(q * N) - 1 ]
```

- p99.9 of N=10,000 → the 9,990th ascending sample (10th largest).
- p10 of N=150 flicks → the 15th ascending sample.
- max → the N-th ascending sample.

This pins the convention the GDD's Proof 3 caveat routed here (R11). A different
convention would require re-deriving the ARM restore implication; it can only
cause unnecessary escalation, never a false pass.

**Sample counts**: AC-53/54: 10,000 ticks per workload after a 600-tick warm-up
(counters reset at warm-up end; first-press lazy init excluded). AC-65: 10,000
injected events per profile. AC-64: 150 flicks per device (5 testers × 30), plus
60 s of scripted retreat-walk per tester for the false-fire bar; the a11y direct
press: 20 scripted presses per device. AC-63: ≥5 testers × ≥30 min.

### 5.4 S_base / S_burst partition and non-emptiness

**Burst definition (event-count-based).** A physics tick is a **burst tick** iff
the capture queue drained **≥3 events** in that tick's capture phase. A tick with
0–2 arrivals is **S_base**. The partition is disjoint; a burst tick is excluded
from S_base.

**Bars (GDD):**

- **S_base**: p99.9 ≤ **1.0 ms** and max ≤ **2.0 ms** per physics tick.
- **S_burst**: max ≤ **4.0 ms**; burst ticks excluded from S_base.
- **Coverage**: S_base must be **≥90% of measured ticks**; a degenerate
  partition fails coverage, not the bar.
- **Non-emptiness (S_burst rider)**: a measured run with **zero burst ticks
  fails the workload-coverage check**; the burst bar never passes vacuously. The
  harness reports the empty population as a coverage failure, not a pass.

W6's 5% burst rate leaves S_base at ~95%, comfortably above 90%. W1–W5/W7 are
mostly S_base; their burst ticks (if any) are labeled, not hidden. The analyzer
prints both populations and the coverage percentage.

**Enqueue cost** (render-path capture): timestamp + O(1) enqueue, measured
separately: **p99.9 ≤ 0.1 ms, max ≤ 0.5 ms**. This is the `_input` callback
span, not the tick pipeline.

**What is instrumented.** The complete per-tick SYS-01 node pipeline: capture-
queue drain (drain-all), F-02/03/04/05/07/08/09/10 evaluation, TR-INP-071
re-assertion, TR-INP-032 ring append, dispatch/ack, and the SYS-29 press/depress
hook **enqueue** side. The vibrator IPC is **outside** the input scope (SYS-29's
budget); AC-70's jank clause is where that cost is gated.

### 5.5 Max-gate breach adjudication

A max-gate breach is not automatically a failure, but it is never silently
ignored:

1. Inspect the per-tick trace. If the breach is a **single OS hiccup** with no
   input-path span > 2.0 ms in the surrounding 100 ticks, re-run the same
   10,000-tick window **once**.
2. A second breach fails the bar. The p99.9 gate is not re-run; it is the
   population gate.
3. Record the trace, the hiccup evidence, and the re-run ID in the evidence
   folder. A breach without a trace is a failure.

AC-70's jank clause uses the same pointer: "breach adjudication is AC-53's ledger
pointer's, not a second policy."

### 5.6 Thermal protocol

- Device cool to start; battery >50%; **not charging**; ambient 20–25°C.
- 20 min continuous play (the workload mix), then measure the **last 5 min**.
- If frame time >20 ms sustained or the device reports >40°C, stop, cool, and
  re-run. Record the thermal state in the manifest.
- A run that throttles mid-measurement is invalid; the re-run is a new folder.
- The thermal protocol is not a bar; it is the condition that makes the bar
  meaningful on mobile.

### 5.7 Harness mechanics

- **Probe**: a dev-only `PerfProbe` autoload samples `Time.get_ticks_usec()` at
  the phase boundaries (phase 0 open, phase 1 capture start/end, phase 2 publish,
  phase 3 gate-entry, phase 4 offers, phase 5 acks, phase 6 expiry). It writes a
  preallocated CSV: tick, phase spans, batch size, population label.
- **Null-pipeline run**: same injection volume, pipeline bypassed, measures the
  probe + injection overhead. The probe overhead must be <0.05 ms p99.9; if not,
  optimize the probe.
- **Analyzer**: reads the CSV, labels S_base/S_burst, computes nearest-rank
  percentiles, prints the coverage percentage and the non-emptiness check.
- **Trace ring**: 600 ticks (10 s @ 60) for post-hoc inspection; it is part of
  the input's preallocated structures, not a new allocation in the hot path.

### 5.8 Monitors, allocation and the control run (AC-54)

**Monitors** (names to verify against 4.7.2 at harness build; the GDD's
`Memory.get_memory_usage` is not used):

| Monitor | Use |
|---|---|
| `Performance.MEMORY_DYNAMIC` | Dynamic heap growth; churn envelope |
| `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` | Net object delta |
| `Performance.OBJECT_RESOURCE_COUNT` | Net resource delta |

**Procedure.** 10,000-tick GUT soak under the workload; warm-up 600 ticks;
counters reset at warm-up end; sample every tick; back-to-back in one process
session with the **workload-no-pipeline control run** (same injection volume,
pipeline bypassed).

**Bars (pipeline run):**

- Net object delta == **0**.
- Net resource delta == **0**.
- Dynamic heap growth ≤ **256 KB** (leak/retention criterion).
- Churn envelope: per-tick sampled max−min of `MEMORY_DYNAMIC` over **any**
  1,000-tick window ≤ **16 KB**.
- The churn envelope is measured on the pipeline run only; it is never
  subtracted from the control run and never compared to the control run's churn.

**Control run bar (standalone):** net object delta == **0** and net resource
delta == **0**, proving the injection itself is allocation-neutral. The control
run has no churn bar beyond its own zero-delta assertion.

**Scope (PA B-1).** The bars cover every SYS-01-owned hot-path structure, each
preallocated and bounded:

| Structure | Bound | Overflow behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Verb slots | 9 (8 body + stinger socket) | registration rejects a 10th |
| Snapshot storage | 9 (one per slot) | fixed |
| Trace ring | 600 ticks | oldest overwritten |
| Haptic enqueue records | 64 | dev assert + production telemetry; not silent coalescing |
| Capture queue | 256 events | dev assert + telemetry; the drain-all policy forbids silent pre-dispatch drops |
| Gate-request queue | 8 | dev assert + telemetry; a gate request is never silently lost |

Nothing else is SYS-01-owned allocation scope; engine-internal allocation
outside these structures is out of scope. **Measurand-vs-scope attribution**: the
memory monitors sample process-wide, so gate scope is attributed by these named
structures; a named-structure high-water mark above its bound fails the test even
if the process-wide delta is zero. The harness logs each structure's high-water
mark in the run manifest.

### 5.9 Haptics-on jank (AC-70's second clause)

GIVEN the reference device with `HAPTIC_GLOBAL_STRENGTH > 0`, WHEN a 12 t/s mash
runs with the haptic stream active for 60 s, THEN no dropped frames occur. The
run config pins the coalescing setting (`HAPTIC_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`, default 50) in
the manifest; the shipped default coalesces roughly half of the 41.7 ms-spaced
edges, so the jank run must use the shipped default, not a debug no-coalescing
mode. Breach adjudication is §5.5's, not a second policy.

### 5.10 AC-65 — the stamp protocol and O1

**GUT half (the gate).**

- Inject events at known sub-tick offsets (0, ¼, ½, ¾ of a tick) with synthetic
  `arrival_usec`; assert `stamp == first logic_tick boundary at or after
  arrival`.
- Fuzz 10,000 events; **zero retroactive stamps**.
- **Freeze arrivals** are excluded from the latency budget and asserted
  separately: they stamp at the first `logic_tick` after unfreeze.
- **Freeze-onset boundary**: the tick in which the freeze request lands is the
  last stamped `logic_tick`; a press on that boundary's capture phase stamps at
  it; a press after it waits.
- **Multi-tick frames**: two physics ticks in one render frame drain all
  captures in the first tick's capture phase; arrival order preserved; no
  retroactive distribution.
- **Same-tick capture/consume**: a capture on tick T can be offered and pulled
  on T (the Early Press's zero stamp-relative delay).

**Device half (conditional, B8).**

- Kept **only if engine item 12 yields OS event time**. With OS event time:
  10,000 events per reference profile in unfrozen gameplay; report
  arrival→stamp **p99.9 ≤ 2 `logic_tick`s and max ≤ 3**; name the pinned input
  flushing setting (item 16) in the harness config.
- Without OS event time: the device half **degrades to the documented
  callback-arrival caveat**; the budget is ADR-owned (TR-INP-076); no device gate.
- The pre-callback queueing detector is deleted (it fired on every correct
  build); remediation on breach is ADR-owned (stamp-policy amendment or
  dispatch-pipeline escalation, OQ#1).

**O1.** AC-18's head says "up to 2"; its parenthetical says "p99.9 ≤ 2 and max ≤
3". The **ratified budget is the parenthetical**: p99.9 ≤ 2, max ≤ 3. AC-18's
GUT test asserts the offer cadence, not the budget; AC-65's device half measures
the budget. The GDD's one-clause correction is tracked in §11; it does not change
the measurement.

### 5.11 GUT half vs device half summary

| Unit | GUT half | Device half |
|---|---|---|
| AC-53 | Pipeline structure; capture callback does only timestamp+enqueue; phase order; S_base/S_burst partition on a synthetic trace; non-emptiness fails on zero bursts | The bars on the reference SKU; enqueue cost; max-gate adjudication |
| AC-54 | 10,000-tick soak; control run; named structures; churn envelope; monitor names verified | — (allocation is a GUT bar; device confirms no jank under load) |
| AC-65 | Exact rule; fuzz; freeze arrivals; freeze-onset; multi-tick; same-tick | Conditional on item 12; p99.9/max; flushing setting named |
| AC-66 | Floor-derived insets; layout arithmetic; gap/reach; mirror; crop | Device-reported insets; query-vs-physical; boundary taps dead |
| AC-74 | The register's verdict table; zero `PROBE-PENDING` | The device items' evidence (2, 12, 13, 15, etc.) |

## 6 · Layout ledger — AC-25 / AC-34 / AC-66 / AC-76

The GDD's per-profile arithmetic lives here (altitude law, review #5). The
audited layout table is the authority; positions are table data, not knobs (B6).
The audit is a GUT test that reads the table + knobs and computes every value
below; a mismatch fails with the pair/region named.

### 6.1 The seven-profile matrix (shipping landscape frame, EX-10)

Floors: mobile cutout surfaces **sides 59 / bottom 48 / top 0 dp**, ceil-rounded
to px; desktop windowed reads **0 on every axis** (window rect IS the safe rect;
NB-G). `k = max(1, min(floor(safe_w/480), floor(safe_h/270)))`.

| Profile | Density | Safe px | Safe dp | `k` | World band px | Bars |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 2400×1080 px | 2.75 | 2074×948 | 754.2×344.7 | 3 | 1440×810 | side 317 px · top/bottom 69 px |
| 1560×720 px | 2.0 | 1324×624 | 662.0×312.0 | 2 | 960×540 | side 182 px · top/bottom 42 px |
| 4K desktop 3840×2160 px | 2.0 | 3840×2160 | 1920.0×1080.0 | 8 | 3840×2160 | none |
| 640×360 dp (1280×720 px) | 2.0 | 1044×624 | 522.0×312.0 | 2 | 960×540 | side 42 px · top/bottom 42 px |
| 1280×800 dp (2560×1600 px) | 2.0 | 2324×1504 | 1162.0×752.0 | 4 | 1920×1080 | side 202 px · top/bottom 212 px |
| 1024×768 dp (2048×1536 px) | 2.0 | 1812×1440 | 906.0×720.0 | 3 | 1440×810 | side 186 px · top/bottom 315 px |
| 1440×720 px (low-H probe) | 2.75 | 1114×588 | 405.1×213.8 | 2 | 960×540 | side 77 px · top/bottom 24 px |
| Safe < 480×270 (crop probe) | 2.0 | e.g. 400×200 | 200×100 | 1 | 480×270 (cropped to 400×200) | crop edge = boundary |

The band is centered in the safe rect by integer division; bars are the
remainder. The 4K desktop profile has no bars because `480·8 = 3840` and
`270·8 = 2160` exactly — the NB-G proof that a desktop floor would phantom-
letterbox a 4K window (k 8→7) is why desktop floors are 0.

### 6.2 Hit rects at the three hit-scales

`hit_px = ceil(max(visual_dp, dp_floor × touch_hit_scale) × density)`; the
bubble is **scale-exempt** (56 dp, pinned `touch_hit_scale = 1.0`). All values
are integers; the ceil is inside F-06 (R13).

**Scale 1.0**

| Profile | Attack 60 | Jump 56 | Dash 48 | Backdash 48 | Pause 48 | Bubble 56 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2400×1080 @2.75 | 165 | 154 | 132 | 132 | 132 | 154 |
| 1560×720 @2.0 | 120 | 112 | 96 | 96 | 96 | 112 |
| 4K @2.0 | 120 | 112 | 96 | 96 | 96 | 112 |
| 640×360 dp @2.0 | 120 | 112 | 96 | 96 | 96 | 112 |
| 1280×800 dp @2.0 | 120 | 112 | 96 | 96 | 96 | 112 |
| 1024×768 dp @2.0 | 120 | 112 | 96 | 96 | 96 | 112 |
| 1440×720 @2.75 | 165 | 154 | 132 | 132 | 132 | 154 |

**Scale 1.25** (gameplay floor 48×1.25 = 60 dp; the bubble stays 56)

| Profile | Attack | Jump | Dash | Backdash | Pause | Bubble |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2400×1080 @2.75 | 165 | 165 | 165 | 165 | 165 | 154 |
| 1560×720 @2.0 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 112 |
| 4K @2.0 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 112 |
| 640×360 dp @2.0 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 112 |
| 1280×800 dp @2.0 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 112 |
| 1024×768 dp @2.0 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 112 |
| 1440×720 @2.75 | 165 | 165 | 165 | 165 | 165 | 154 |

**Scale 1.5** (gameplay floor 48×1.5 = 72 dp; the bubble stays 56)

| Profile | Attack | Jump | Dash | Backdash | Pause | Bubble |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2400×1080 @2.75 | 198 | 198 | 198 | 198 | 198 | 154 |
| 1560×720 @2.0 | 144 | 144 | 144 | 144 | 144 | 112 |

**Assertions per row**: `hit_px` is an integer; `hit_px ≥ visual`; the pre-round
identity `hit_px / density ≥ max(visual_dp, floor × scale)` holds; the bubble
satisfies its unscaled 56 dp at every scale; no hit rect is smaller than its
visual. The fractional-density case (2.625, a real Android panel class) is
tested separately: Attack 60 dp → 157.5 → **158 px**; `158 / 2.625 ≈ 60.19 ≥ 60`;
ceil overshoot 0.5 px ≤ 1 px.

### 6.3 Pairwise gaps, reach disc and V21

**Pairwise center distances** (profile-invariant at the audited table; all six
pairs among the four gameplay sockets):

| Pair | Center distance dp | Requirement at 1.5 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Attack–Jump | 87.32 | 36 + 36 + 12 = 84 |
| Attack–Dash | 87.48 | 84 |
| Attack–Backdash | 98.41 | 84 |
| Jump–Dash | 151.86 | 84 |
| Jump–Backdash | 90.09 | 84 |
| Dash–Backdash | 97.53 | 84 |

The minimum 87.32 ≥ 84; the audited table passes. Pause pairs are
profile-dependent (the pause is anchored to the stick-side top corner); they are
computed per profile and must satisfy `r1 + r2 + 12` at 1.5 (pause radius 36).
The pause is exempt from the reach disc but not from the gap audit (R-9).

**Reach disc** (center at the cluster corner; radius 200 dp):

| Control | Edge-anchored distance dp | Inside 200? |
|---|---:|---|
| Attack | 92.2 | yes |
| Jump | 147.5 | yes |
| Dash | 162.1 | yes |
| a11y Backdash | 189.6 | yes (the max; the 190 floor of the knob range is why the default is 200) |
| Pause | profile-dependent | **exempt** (R-9; still in the gap audit) |

**V21 runtime fit** (per profile, at the active hit-scale):
`H_safe ≥ 142 + max(56, 48 × scale) / 2` → **170 dp at 1.0**, **178 dp at 1.5**.
The low-H probe reaches `H_safe ≈ 213.8 dp` (588/2.75), which fits 178; the
640×360 dp profile reaches 312 dp; all matrix profiles pass. The crop probe may
fail V21; it is flagged, telemetry logs it, and the a11y pause-menu actions
(Interact, Toggle-Crouch) plus the AC-64 a11y Backdash button cover reachability.
V21 is **not a config clamp**; it is a runtime layout flag.

### 6.4 Mirror, crop and dead bars

**Edge convention.** `Rect2i.end` is exclusive (`position + size`); the layout
audit anchors `x_in`/`y_up` to that exclusive edge and clamps each hit rect's far
edge to `end − 1`. The 1 px difference is not a tolerance: the audit computes the
same convention for every profile, and a hit rect that crosses `end − 1` fails.

**Mirror.** The canonical frame is `(x_in, y_up)` from the right/bottom safe
edges. `MIRROR` maps `x_px = safe_rect.position.x + x_in × density` (unmirrored:
`safe_rect.end.x - x_in × density`); the stick zone swaps to the right 42%; the
pause moves to the top-right (it mirrors with the stick); the bubble's interior
offset and leader line reflect in x; the reach disc center moves to the left
cluster corner. The audit re-runs all six pairs, the reach, V19/V21 and the
bubble cascade mirrored. A live touch keeps its binding; the world moved, not the
order.

**Crop.** When `safe_w < 480` or `safe_h < 270`, `k = 1`; the band is
`480×270` center-cropped to `visible_band = band ∩ safe`; `art_origin =
(visible_band.position - band_origin) / k`; the screen→art transform uses
`visible_band` and `art_origin`; taps outside are dead; hit rects clip to the
visible region. The crop edge behaves as the viewport boundary (TR-INP-063).

**Dead bars.** Every bar surface (side and top/bottom) is a dead world-layer tap.
The world layer binds only inside `visible_band`; HUD controls may sit over a bar
because they are on the native layer; the bubble stays inside `visible_band` and
never straddles a bar's world-area edge.

### 6.5 AC-25 / AC-66 / AC-34 / AC-76 execution

| Unit | GUT half | Device half |
|---|---|---|
| AC-25 | All seven profiles; every hit rect at 1.0/1.25/1.5; integrality; pre-round identity; scale-exempt bubble; no hit < visual; the `k` band never displaces a registered region; the screen→art mapping exact under the D1 model (contingent on item 8) | — |
| AC-66 | Floor-derived insets; the seven-profile centers/radii/gaps; reach; V21; mirror; dead bars; the crop; the bubble cascade | Device-reported insets; query-vs-physical; taps at the inset boundary dead; V21 per profile |
| AC-34 | Pairwise gaps; reach; bubble clearances; pause scaling; mirror; the audited table | — |
| AC-76 | Bubble fallback cascade at 1.0 and 1.5; the smallest profile (640×360); never inside the movement zone; mirrored | The 1.5 extended-leader case on device |

The audit is a **test**, not a spreadsheet: it reads the audited table + the
knobs, computes the values above, and fails with the pair/region and the two
numbers that disagree. The per-profile arithmetic in this section is the expected
value set; a change to the table or a knob re-runs the audit.

### 6.6 The dp/mm boundary

Target sizes are dp/mm, never art pixels. The dp→px bridge is
`screen_density`; the mm path has no bridge (a documented gap: the GDD's "dp/mm"
claim is dp-only at MVP). The bubble's 56 dp, the 48/44 dp floors and the
`TOUCH_HIT_SCALE` values are dp; the world's 480×270 is art units; the
`SubViewport` is physical px. No third unit enters the transform.

### 6.7 The `k`/band identity

For every profile: `band_px = 480k × 270k`; `k = max(1, min(floor(safe_w/480),
floor(safe_h/270)))`; the band is centered; the bars are the remainder. The
identity `band_px ≤ safe_rect.size` holds by construction for `k ≥ 1` when the
safe rect is at least 480×270; in the crop case, `k = 1` and the visible band is
the intersection. The screen→art transform is the inverse of the band placement
plus the camera zoom: `art = (screen - visible_band.position)/k + art_origin`,
floor. A one-pixel band-centering error is a test failure, not a tolerance.

## 7 · Device matrix and AC-64 producibility protocol

### 7.1 Device matrix

The matrix is the GDD's AC-27/AC-64 matrix, expanded to the seven layout profiles
plus the crop probe. Each run manifest records the exact SKU, OS build, density,
safe rect, `k`, hit-scale and mirror state.

| Class | Profile(s) | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Android small phone | 640×360 dp @2.0; 1560×720 px @2.0 | Smallest matrix profile; V21; cluster fit |
| Android large phone | 2400×1080 px @2.75 | Shipping flagship; cutout sides 59 dp |
| Android tablet | 1280×800 dp @2.0 (16:10) | Top/bottom bars; k=4 |
| iPad | 1024×768 dp @2.0 (4:3) | Top/bottom bars; k=3 |
| iPhone | 1560×720 px @2.0 class; 2400×1080 class | iOS safe area + haptics caveat |
| Low-H probe | 1440×720 px @2.75 | Android display-size scaling; V21 stress |
| Desktop 4K | 3840×2160 @2.0 windowed | No floors; k=8; no bars |
| Crop probe | safe < 480×270 | k=1; crop; dead edges |

The **touch-cancel** and **focus-loss** items run on every mobile class; the
**gamepad** items run on the desktop/PC class with at least two pad families.

### 7.2 AC-64 — the producibility protocol

**Cohort.** ≥5 uncoached testers per device class; 30 flicks each = **150 flicks
per device**; scripted instruction, **no demonstration**. The tester is told
"flick back twice, quickly" and nothing else; the raw stick trace is recorded.

**Bars.**

| Bar | Measurement | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| Crossing | ≥90% of flicks peak ≥ `BAND_WALK_ENTER` | per device |
| Weak tail | pooled per-device **p10** of peaks ≥ `BAND_WALK_ENTER` + 0.05 | per device |
| In-window | ≥85% of sequences have press2 − press1 ≤ `BACKDASH_TAP_WINDOW_MS` | per device |
| False fire | ≤1 unintended fire per tester per 60 s of scripted retreat-walk, replayed through F-07 | per device |
| End-to-end | ≥80% of in-window sequences produce an actual F-07 fire (logged traces replayed) | per device |
| A11y direct | 100% of 20 scripted a11y presses complete | per device |

**Percentile convention**: nearest-rank; p10 of 150 = the 15th ascending sample.
The p10 is **pooled per device**, not per tester. The crossing bar and the p10
bar are the two **ARM-fixable** classes; the in-window, false-fire, end-to-end
and a11y bars are timing/detector fit and are gated separately.

**ARM fallback (evidence-gated).** If a device fails either ARM-fixable bar:

```
BACKDASH_ARM_MAG = min over failing devices of (p10_device - 0.05)
then V16 clamp: BACKDASH_ARM_MAG ≥ BAND_CREEP_ENTER + 0.05 (0.30 at defaults)
the post-clamp value is the one tested
```

- The promoted value must sit **strictly below** every failing device's p10 so
  the p10 bar is satisfiable, not equal to it.
- If the derivation is below the V16 floor, that is the **by-design ESCALATE
  corner**: the device is not ARM-fixable; AC-64's fallback evaluation escalates
  to the a11y Backdash button route. The knob never clamps upward past the
  derivation to fake a pass.
- The fallback is for the two ARM-fixable bars only; it does not rescue the
  in-window/false-fire/end-to-end bars.

**Evidence**: raw trace per flick; the replay log for false-fire/end-to-end; the
per-device p10 table; the ARM derivation arithmetic; the a11y press count. Path:
`production/qa/evidence/sys01/ac64/<device>/`.

### 7.3 AC-63 — the coded playtest protocol

**Cohort**: ≥5 mixed-rig testers (touch-native + PC), each ≥30 min; the interview
script is fixed before the session; the facilitator does not demonstrate.

**Coding.** Two facilitators independently code the transcripts **per statement**
(the coding unit). Agreement ≥90% per statement; **Cohen's kappa ≥0.7** computed
per statement across all subjects. The 20-statement floor is deleted;
transcript-level kappa on N=5 is near-meaningless. Disagreements are adjudicated
by the definition list, never by taste.

**Codes.**

| Question | Code | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 "Describe the controls to a friend" | *trust-code* | contains any of {always does what I mean / obeys / listens / trust / never lost a press} and none of {lag / delay / late / response time}; "slow" is **not** forbidden |
| Q1 negation | bidirectional | a negated forbidden term within 3 tokens of its subject does **not** block trust-code ("never lag"); a negated trust term **does** block ("never obeys me"); set-membership idioms ("never lost a press") are evaluated first |
| Q2 "Describe a moment a press felt off" | *early-press observation* | pressing before the visible hit and the game answering; **non-gating observation**; the mash-dominance probe is the GUT sweep on AC-20's harness at Combat's review |
| Q3 "Describe your last death — what did you press?" | *lag-attribution* | startup frames named as lag = failure signal |
| Q4 "Name anything you pressed that did nothing" | *drop rate* | reports per session-minute, alongside the negation counts; feeds AC-02's probe |

**Reporting**: negation counts, drop rate per session-minute, per-statement
agreement, kappa. **Evidence**: transcripts (anonymized), the two coding sheets,
the adjudication log, the kappa computation. Path:
`production/session-logs/playtest-sys01-ac63-<date>/`.

**Sign-off**: creative-director + qa-lead. AC-63 is MVP-lock; it does not run in
the smoke gate.

## 8 · MVP device protocols

Each protocol below is the AC's GIVEN/WHEN/THEN reduced to the measurement; the
GDD text is authoritative. All runs use the matrix in §7.1 and the run manifest
in §3.6.

### 8.1 AC-12 — mirrored play

Left-handed tester with `MIRROR` on completes the MVP core loop on a real device;
zero input failures in the session log (failure = press with no delivery, wrong
verb, double-fire, lost state). Evidence: session log + video. NB-E unit: device.

### 8.2 AC-27 — multi-touch, palm, bars

Three fingers play move + Jump + Attack concurrently; a stick + bubble-finger pair
works simultaneously; a palm/edge touch on the letterbox or outside every zone
binds dead (no capture, no error, no haptic). Evidence: video + touch trace.

### 8.3 AC-36 / AC-37 — OS cancel and density rescale

- **AC-36 (MVP stick/crouch clause)**: OS-cancel a stick touch and a crouch
  guard; the stick releases, the guard resets; a cancelled touch is never a
  signed order. The chip clause is VS.
- **AC-37 (MVP stick/scale clause)**: density/scale rescale mid-stick-touch; no
  commit/region move under a stationary finger; the hold keeps its binding;
  regions re-register correctly. The chip clause is VS.

### 8.4 AC-45 — blur and platform Back

Blur mid-fight forces Paused from any context; restore returns to Paused, never
straight to Gameplay; Back in Gameplay opens Pause; Back elsewhere maps to that
context's back; blur disposes touch-originated held states while KB/pad held
states persist (EX-3). iOS: blur + on-screen controls only; Back is Android-only.

### 8.5 AC-47 / AC-48 / AC-52 — a11y scale, crouch toggle, AccessKit

- **AC-47**: `TOUCH_HIT_SCALE` 1.25 then 1.5; scaling is hit-only; 48/44 dp
  floors hold; each overlap touchdown binds exactly one region per z-order.
- **AC-48**: toggle crouch per rig (touch confirmed tap; button single press);
  crouch-walk; attack from crouch; Jump clears; re-crouch; a 31° release latches;
  a release outside the exit cone cancels.
- **AC-52**: pause → Recalibration → help overlay; AccessKit name/role; the
  bubble's accessible name equals its label; keyboard focus order; the help
  overlay documents the three fixed touch semantics and the backdash gesture;
  no hover-only interaction. Screen-reader claim is menu-scoped.

### 8.6 AC-50 / AC-70 — haptics

- **AC-50**: each mapped event at strength 1.0 then 0; the correct weight at 1.0;
  at 0 every haptic is silent **where the platform allows**; the held-state
  visual carries the meaning. iOS carve-out is AC-70's.
- **AC-70 capability-rendition**: per device class (iOS stock API, Android 26+,
  Android <26, no-vibrator), the best available rendition fires; haptics-off is
  silent where the platform allows.
- **AC-70 haptics-on jank**: §5.9.

### 8.7 AC-69 — a11y gestures (non-chip clauses)

Backdash button publishes a direct intent (single-tick, body-free, direction =
−facing, resets a mid-pattern gesture; dual-source same-tick coalesces to one
intent); toggle-crouch latches on the confirmed tap while Jump clears; pause-menu
Toggle-Crouch latches/unlatches in both modes; Jump clears in both modes. The chip
clause is VS.

### 8.8 AC-74 — the 16-item register

The GUT half checks the register's verdict table and that zero items are
`PROBE-PENDING` before the first story. The device half runs the device items'
evidence (2, 12, 13, 15, etc.). The ADR-0001 §16 table is the source.

## 9 · VS-gated clauses (deferred)

The seven VS units run when the chip and Stinger go live. The ledger rows exist
now; the protocols are outlined so the future work has a home.

| Unit | Protocol outline |
|---|---|
| AC-33 chip clause | Chip hold crosses `CHIP_HOLD_COMMIT_MS` during Gameplay hit-stop; commits with age frozen until resume; the decision/delivery split (EX-15) |
| AC-35 | Chip release at threshold −0.1 / exactly threshold / slide-off / blur; commit at the threshold, stamp at the commit tick, no retroactive touchdown |
| AC-36 chip clause | OS-cancel a chip hold; never commits on return |
| AC-37 chip clause | Density/scale rescale mid-chip-hold; binding-based release; no commit from region movement |
| AC-42 | VS Stinger: quarter-spin + attack; ↓↘→ + attack; exactly one Stinger, no plain attack; tolerance bracket |
| AC-60 chip clause | Chip tap with zero items is a silent no-op; HUD never consumes gameplay touches |
| AC-69 chip clause | `CHIP_TAP_COMMIT_MS` exactly commits, 0.1 below does not |

The VS gate is not part of MVP hand-off; a VS failure does not block the MVP
lock, but it blocks the VS milestone.

## 11 · O1 register — the carried obligation

**O1 (AC-18).** The stamp-budget head says "arrival→stamp may consume up to 2
`logic_tick`s" while its own parenthetical says "p99.9 ≤ 2 **and** max ≤ 3".
The clause disagrees with itself.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Ratified budget** | **p99.9 ≤ 2 `logic_ticks`, max ≤ 3** (the parenthetical; TR-INP-076/AC-65) |
| **Measured by** | AC-65's device half (conditional on engine item 12 yielding OS event time); otherwise the callback-arrival caveat and the budget is ADR-owned |
| **Not measured by** | AC-18's GUT test — it asserts the Early Press offer cadence (including the stamp tick), not the budget |
| **GDD correction** | One clause under the unfrozen regime: "may consume up to 3 `logic_ticks` (p99.9 ≤ 2, max ≤ 3)" or equivalent; ordinary reviewed edit |
| **Verification of the correction** | Re-run the machine cross-reference membership audit (the AC-18 row + the stem sweep) + a qa-lead spot-check on the changed site |
| **Carried by** | ADR-0001's Acceptance Record + this plan's AC-65 protocol |
| **Blocks?** | No. It does not block the unfreeze, the ADR acceptance, or the ledger; it blocks only its own text. It does not change the measurement. |

**Why this plan carries it.** The #10 record routed O1 to "ADR Acceptance + the
QA plan's AC-65 protocol". The ADR ratifies the parenthetical; this plan measures
it. The AC-18 row in the ledger (row 19) is smoke-gated as a whole AC; the budget
is not an AC-18 GUT claim. The AC-65 row (row 76) is the device half; its
protocol is §5.10.

**Bookkeeping note (not an obligation).** The GDD's gate-manifest parenthetical
still says the QA plan's ledger is "hard-blocked until #9"; the #10 record
supersedes that condition (the ledger is printed here under the #10 authority).
A one-clause bookkeeping edit is recommended when the AC-18 fix lands; it is not
a new obligation and does not change the 96-unit partition.

### 12.3 What would invalidate this plan

- A change to the GDD's gate manifest or AC census that changes the 96-unit
  partition without a re-derivation.
- A change to the audited layout table or a knob that invalidates §6's
  arithmetic without re-running the audit.
- A change to the ADR's pipeline order or clock law that invalidates §5's
  measurement.
- An engine-version change (4.7.2 → another) that invalidates the probe
  register.
- A new AC or a deleted AC without a ledger re-derivation.

In any of these cases, this plan is **superseded**, not silently patched. The
re-derivation is a new artifact; the old one stays for the audit trail.

## 13 · Definition of done and sign-off

### 13.1 Unit-level DoD

A ledger unit is **done** when ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] The evidence folder exists at the named path; the run manifest is the
      first file.
- [ ] The unit's AC text (or clause) is verified by the evidence; the verdict is
      PASS, not "looks fine".
- [ ] The evidence names the build hash, device/profile, density, `k`, hit-scale
      and mirror state.
- [ ] No regression in the same gate's other units.
- [ ] The ledger row is unchanged (or the plan is superseded with a new
      derivation).
- [ ] The sign-off is recorded (qa-lead for smoke/device; creative-director +
      qa-lead for lock; qa-lead + design for VS).

### 13.2 Gate-level DoD

- **Smoke gate** — "input is ready for QA hand-off": all 67 smoke units pass;
  the GDD's 31-AC spine is green; the one device pass is clean; the probe
  register is closed. Sign-off: qa-lead.
- **MVP device gate** — all 19 device units pass on the matrix; the run manifests
  are complete; the device-lab lead signs the matrix. Sign-off: qa-lead +
  device-lab lead.
- **MVP-lock gate** — AC-02, AC-63, AC-64 pass; the producibility/playtest
  evidence is reviewed; no ARM fallback is hiding a non-ARM failure. Sign-off:
  creative-director + qa-lead.
- **VS gate** — the seven VS units pass when the chip/Stinger go live. Sign-off:
  qa-lead + design.

### 13.3 Sign-off record

| Gate | Verdict | Date | Sign-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Probe register (AC-74) | ☐ open / ☐ closed | | godot-specialist |
| MVP smoke | ☐ pass / ☐ fail | | qa-lead |

| MVP-lock | ☐ pass / ☐ fail | | creative-director + qa-lead |

**Release note.** The smoke gate is not the MVP lock. A green smoke gate means
"input is ready for QA hand-off"; the MVP lock still needs the device gate and
the three lock units. Do not merge these claims.

### 14.6 How to re-derive the ledger

1. Read the GDD's gate manifest (the four gates) and every AC's inline tag /
   `Gate split` sentence.
2. Enumerate AC-01…AC-79; split the 14 split ACs into their clauses.
3. Assign each `(AC, clause)` to exactly one gate: lock (AC-02/63/64), VS (the
   chip/Stinger clauses + AC-42), device (the 17 `[DEVICE]`-tagged ACs' device
   clauses, **including** the four NB-E units), smoke (the rest).
4. Count: 67 + 19 + 3 + 7 = 96. If the count differs, the manifest or an inline
   tag changed; stop and re-derive, do not patch.
5. Print the table; verify no `(AC, clause)` pair appears twice; verify every
   `[DEVICE]`-tagged AC is accounted for.

This is the same derivation the #9 qa-lead and the #8 repair performed; the plan
is the fifth deterministic record. The ledger is the **operational** artifact;
the GDD remains the design authority.
